title: Frontend: close coverage to 90% gate, verify Storybook + no-network invariants
description: Closing pass once every frontend-* feature task has landed: run the real coverage gate across the whole app, close any gaps, and verify the cross-cutting invariants (no live network calls, Storybook builds clean) hold for the app as a whole, not just per-task. Mirrors the backend's check-coverage/test-90 skill pair, applied here as one task since there's no dedicated frontend skill yet.

checklist.step: Run `npm run test:coverage` (vitest --coverage) against the full app; identify every file below the 90% lines/branches/functions/statements threshold from docs/architecture/Testing.md.

Write the missing tests to close each gap — prefer testing real behavior (an interaction, a rendered error state) over trivial assertions that only exist to move a number, per Testing.md's 'What 90% Coverage Does Not Guarantee' section.
Grep the whole frontend/ test suite for any accidental real network call (a bare fetch()/axios call not going through MSW, or a test missing its MSW handler) — fix any found.

Confirm `npm run build-storybook` still succeeds and every components/common/ component has both a test and a story (re-verify frontend-common-components' bar holds after all feature work landed, since a later task could have quietly skipped it).
Confirm `npm run build` (production build) succeeds with no TypeScript errors.

decisions.decision: Closed StockDetailPage.tsx's branch-coverage gap (88.88% → 100%) by adding a test that renders it under a route with no `:ticker` param, asserting the `ticker || 'Stock Detail'` header fallback and that useStockAnalysis's `enabled: ticker.length > 0` guard skips the query (no loading/error UI renders). Left two other pre-existing sub-90%-file lines uncovered on purpose rather than fake-covering them: PositionsTable.tsx:87 (`if (!pendingDelete) return` in handleConfirmDelete) and PriceChart.tsx:112 (`if (finiteBars.length === 0) return` in the chart-creation effect) are both TypeScript-narrowing guards that are provably unreachable through any real user interaction — MUI's Dialog unmounts its Confirm button while closed (so handleConfirmDelete can only ever fire with pendingDelete already set), and PriceChart's own `hasBars` (identical filter) gates whether the chart container even renders, so the effect's `!container` branch always fires first when there are zero finite bars. Writing a test to hit either would mean fabricating an app state that can't occur, which Testing.md's 'What 90% Coverage Does Not Guarantee' and this skill's step 4 both flag as not meeting the bar in spirit. Both files (94.44%/92.85% and 97.43%/95.83% resp.) and the suite overall (99.43%/99.21%/100%/99.41%) already clear every dimension of the 90% gate by a wide margin, so no coverage shortfall remains that these two lines would need to close.
decisions.rationale: Alternative considered and rejected: deleting the two guards to eliminate the branches entirely. Rejected because they're not dead code in the sense of no code path ever reaching the surrounding function — they're required for TypeScript's null-narrowing given `useParams`/local nullable state typing, and removing them would trade a harmless always-false guard for a runtime crash risk if the surrounding component's rendering logic is ever refactored in a way that breaks the current invariant. Keeping the defensive guard (undocumented previously) plus this decision entry is safer than deleting real safety code just to chase a per-file number the gate doesn't actually require.
